title: Ateneo Law Journal Honors CJ Teehankee
primary_topics: Remarks at the launch of the special edition of the Ateneo Law Journal honoring the 100th birthday of CJ Claudio Teehankee, July 10, 2019 -- on behalf of the Claudio Teehankee Foundation
The distinction between bar exam topnotchers (who memorize) and law journal editors (who analyze, criticize and improvise) -- and why the latter become social engineers who build just societies
CJ Teehankee as the embodiment of the social engineer ideal: summa cum laude and bar topnotcher who was not just a legal technician but reached for the stars to render justice via the rule of law
FLP's dissertation writing contest as the institutional equivalent of law journal writing -- training law students from legal technicians into social engineers
sub_topics: Octogenarian jokes opener: Reinhold Niebuhr's serenity prayer (age 20) vs. the senility prayer (age 80: 'grant me the senility to forget the people I never liked'); Frank Laubach's 'Life Begins at 80' -- 'at 70, people are mad at you for everything; at 80, you have a perfect excuse, no matter what you do'

The Ateneo Law Journal special edition: launched on behalf of the Claudio Teehankee Foundation; produced by the students of Ateneo de Manila School of Law; Board of Editors thanked; CJP's extemporaneous speech at the 25th Death Anniversary of CJ Teehankee is published with additions by Issue Editor Jason Sy

CJP's previous Forewords for the Ateneo Law Journal: twice invited -- once by Lead Editor Jewelle Santos (who was also a Claudio Teehankee Foundation scholar) and once by Lead Editor Angelo Herbosa (current volume's lead editor, separately); both times satisfied with the diligence, intelligence and excellence of the editors

Bar exam vs. law journal distinction: bar exam requires memorization -- 'to top the bar exams, you must read and reread... the Constitution, the codes, the Rules of Court and all the damn statutes over and over... till the words are erased from the pages'; journal editors must analyze, criticize and improvise -- 'instead of being mere legal robots who parrot laws and decisions word-for-word'

The transformation from legal technician to social engineer: schemers and users of the text → critical thinkers and innovators who search for loftier purposes and intents; commercial interests and private causes → public welfare and social edifice-building; literal interpretation → liberal interpretation to fulfill ultimate ends of justice

CJ Teehankee's profile: graduated summa cum laude and topped bar exams (pure legal technician credentials); but 'he was not just a legal technician repairing his clients' wares -- he was a social engineer who reached out to the stars to render justice via the all-encompassing rule of law'; courageous national hero buried at Libingan ng mga Bayani
Ateneo Law School's institutional identity: produces law scholars and bar topnotchers who 'transcend legal technicalities to become engineers and builders of just societies'

FLP connection: law students should not only top academic studies and bar exams but should also be competent writers, 'to transform them from being mere legal technicians who trouble shoot the rickety structures of their clients to being social engineers who construct durable and unbreakable institutions for the nation'; FLP awards 20 law scholarships + dissertation writing contest (25 prizes from P20,000 to P300,000)

stances.claim: Law journal editors and writers are more valuable to society than bar exam topnotchers because they are trained to analyze, criticize and improvise the law -- becoming social engineers who build just societies -- rather than merely memorize and recite it for private client advantage. The bar exam produces legal technicians; the law journal produces social engineers.
stances.rhetorical_move: bar-exam-vs-law-journal dichotomy as a values argument for the FLP dissertation contest program
stances.confidence: asserted as CJP's governing philosophy of legal education

stances.claim: CJ Teehankee embodies the synthesis: he had the technical credentials (summa cum laude, bar topnotcher) but transcended them to become a social engineer 'who reached out to the stars to render justice via the all-encompassing rule of law.' He is the answer to those who think the bar exam is the ceiling of legal achievement.
stances.rhetorical_move: Teehankee-as-proof-of-synthesis: technical excellence as the foundation, not the ceiling, of social engineering

stances.claim: FLP's dissertation writing contest (25 prizes from P20,000 to P300,000) is the institutional equivalent of law journal training -- it produces the same analytical and persuasive writers who will become the social engineers and builders of just societies, alongside the bar topnotchers produced by the scholarship program.
stances.rhetorical_move: FLP-as-institutional-social-engineering-vehicle: the dissertation contest is explicitly framed as law journal-equivalent training

notable_anecdotes: The senility prayer (vs. the serenity prayer): at age 20, CJP's favorite prayer was Niebuhr's 'Lord, grant me the courage to change the things I can, the serenity to accept the things I cannot change, and the wisdom to know the difference.' Now at 80+: 'Lord, grant me the senility to forget the people I never liked, the good fortune to run into the people I do, and the eyesight to tell the difference.'

Frank Laubach's 'Life Begins at 80': 'Once you reach 80, everyone wants to carry your baggage and help you up the steps... Being 80 is a lot better than being 70. At 70, people are mad at you for everything. At 80, you have a perfect excuse, no matter what you do. If you act foolishly, it's your second childhood.'

The bar reviewer's instruction quoted: 'To top the bar exams, you must read and reread and reread the Constitution, the codes, the Rules of Court and all the damn statutes over and over, over and over till the words are erased from the pages.' -- The vivid contrast with the law journal's analytical approach.
Jewelle Santos: past Ateneo Law Journal Lead Editor who was also a Claudio Teehankee Foundation scholar -- connecting the two institutions that the speech is bridging.

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered July 10, 2019 at the launch of the Ateneo Law Journal special edition honoring CJ Claudio Teehankee's 100th birthday, this speech by CJP -- on behalf of the Claudio Teehankee Foundation -- opens with two self-deprecating octogenarian jokes: Reinhold Niebuhr's serenity prayer transformed at age 80 into 'the senility prayer' ('Lord, grant me the senility to forget the people I never liked'), and Frank Laubach's 'Life Begins at 80' ('at 70, people are mad at you for everything; at 80, you have a perfect excuse'). The substantive argument draws a sharp distinction between bar exam excellence (memorization: 'read and reread... till the words are erased from the pages' -- producing 'mere legal robots who parrot laws and decisions word-for-word') and law journal editing and writing (analysis, criticism and improvisation -- producing 'social engineers who view the law not as an end by itself, but as an instrument in the building of a just society'). CJ Teehankee embodies the synthesis: summa cum laude and bar topnotcher, but not merely a legal technician -- 'he was a social engineer who reached out to the stars to render justice via the all-encompassing rule of law,' a courageous national hero deservingly buried at Libingan ng mga Bayani. CJP notes the Ateneo Law Journal holds a special place in his heart, having written Forewords twice -- once for Lead Editor Jewelle Santos (also a Teehankee Foundation scholar) and once for Lead Editor Angelo Herbosa. He closes by linking FLP's dissertation writing contest (25 prizes from P20,000 to P300,000) to this same social-engineering aspiration: training law students to become, alongside bar topnotchers, 'social engineers who construct durable and unbreakable institutions for the nation.'
